REVIEW:
# Review: Pickleball Conversion Proposal

The draft is strong. It makes a clear conditional recommendation, the arithmetic is correct ($96k + $38k = $134k; $150k − $134k = $16k; 48 × $360 ≈ $17,300), and it is candid about the cost to tennis. It covers nearly every fact in the brief and runs about 500–530 words, which is within the target. The fixes below are mostly small, but the first two affect accuracy.

## Must fix

**1. The "7 of our 8 courts" figure is unsupported.**
The brief gives 88% peak tennis use but doesn't say whether that applies to all 8 courts or to the 6 courts not shared with pickleball. The shared courts are fully booked by pickleball at peak, so 88% of 6 courts is the likelier reading. That works out to about 5.3 courts of demand, not 7. Under that reading, 5 tennis-only courts fall only slightly short, and the draft overstates the loss. Either confirm what the 88% refers to, or drop the conversion to a court count:

> "Tennis courts are 88% booked at peak times (6 to 9 p.m. on weekdays and weekend mornings), and several members already struggle to book. With five tennis courts instead of eight, some members will lose peak-time play."

**2. Remove the stray `##` at the end.**
The document ends with `---` followed by an empty heading, which looks like a leftover artifact.

## Should fix

**3. Say that the board is split, and say who "I" is.**
The brief says the *board* is divided: two long-standing board members oppose the conversion, and the treasurer supports it. The draft refers only to "long-standing members" and is written in the first person without saying who the author is. Members voting at an AGM should know whether this is a board recommendation, a majority view, or one director's proposal. For example: "The board is divided. Two long-standing directors believe…; the treasurer notes…" Then make clear whose recommendation follows.

**4. Show the revenue risk on the tennis side.**
The financial case counts the $17,300 gain but leaves out tennis dues. At $520 each, losing about 33 tennis members would cancel out the waitlist gain. Tennis is already shrinking by about 12 members a year (3% of 410). One sentence on this would make the case more honest and harder to dismiss. It could also use the 410 / 230 membership split, which the draft currently omits.

**5. "Admitting all of them" assumes capacity.**
Add a short qualifier, such as "with 12 dedicated courts, the club could admit the waiting list," so it's clear the $17,300 depends on the new courts.

## Worth considering

- **Phased construction doesn't solve the 2027 roof problem.** Phasing changes when the money is spent, not how much. Because the roof is due the same year, phasing helps only if the spending crosses into a later financial year. Consider listing it last or adding that caveat.
- **The timeline leaves out the follow-up member votes.** The funding plan and the peak-hour booking policy both go back to members. Say whether that happens at a special general meeting before construction, since it could push construction past July.
- **The high-school scheduling line is now redundant.** A council decision around July means construction would fall outside March–May anyway. You could keep it as reassurance ("which keeps construction clear of…") rather than as a separate scheduling commitment.
- **Noise certification timing.** It may help to note that the noise condition matters most because peak play (6–9 p.m.) falls entirely within the ordinance's after-6 p.m. limit. This strengthens the case for making the condition non-negotiable.

## Fact check against the brief

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| 3 courts → 12 pickleball, $96k | ✓ |
| 61 dB measured vs 55 dB limit after 6 p.m., 40 m, 2 complaints | ✓ |
| $38k fencing, $150k reserve, $90k roof in 2027 | ✓ |
| Lease "primary use" clause, ~4-month council vote | ✓ |
| 40% pickleball growth, ~3%/yr tennis decline | ✓ |
| 48 waitlist, $360 pickleball dues | ✓ |
| 88% peak / 31% off-peak use | ✓ (but see item 1) |
| High-school team, March–May weekday afternoons; 6-week build | ✓ |
| 640 / 410 / 230 members; $520 tennis dues | ✗ Omitted |
| Board is split | ✗ Recast as "members" |
